title: 是 links two nouns
short: A 是 B means A is B.
body: 是 joins a noun to a noun: 我是學生, I am a student. It is not used before adjectives, so "I am busy" is 我很忙, not 我是忙.

title: 嗎 makes a yes or no question
short: Add 嗎 to the end of a statement.
body: Word order stays the same as the statement. 你是老師 is a statement, and 你是老師嗎 asks whether you are a teacher.

title: 不 negates
short: Put 不 before a verb or adjective.
body: 不 is the everyday negative for the present, for habits and for what you will or won't do: 我不喝茶, I don't drink tea. Its one exception is 有, which takes 沒.

title: 的 links a describer to a noun
body: Whatever comes before 的 describes what comes after it: 我的書, my book. With close relationships it is often dropped: 我媽媽, my mum.

title: 很 before adjectives
body: Adjectives act as verbs in Chinese, so they need no 是. A plain adjective can sound like a comparison, so 很 is usually added even when it doesn't really mean "very": 他很高, he is tall.

title: 有 means have and there is
short: 有 for having, 沒有 for not having.
body: 有 covers both possession and existence: 我有貓, I have a cat. Negate it only with 沒, never 不.

title: Question words stay in place
short: Put 什麼 where the answer would go.
body: Chinese doesn't move question words to the front. You drink tea is 你喝茶. What do you drink is 你喝什麼, with 什麼 sitting where 茶 was.

title: 也 and 都 go before the verb
short: Subject + 也 or 都 + verb.
body: 也 means also and 都 means all or both. Both go after the subject and before the verb, never at the front of a sentence: 我也去, I'm going too.

title: 在 for location
body: 在 says where something is: 他在家, he is at home. It can also come before a verb to say where something happens: 我在學校吃飯.

title: 想 and 要 for wanting
short: 想 is would like, 要 is want or will.
body: Both go before a verb. 我想喝水 is softer, I'd like some water. 我要喝水 is firmer, I want water, and 要 can also mean something is going to happen.

title: 了 after an action
short: Verb + 了 marks a completed action.
body: 了 isn't simply a past tense. After a verb it says the action was completed: 我吃了三個蘋果. Negate past actions with 沒 and drop the 了: 我沒吃.

title: 沒 negates the past
short: 沒 + verb means it didn't happen.
body: 不 refuses or denies a habit, 沒 says something hasn't happened: 我沒去, I didn't go. Compare 我不去, I'm not going.

title: 會, 能 and 可以
body: 會 is a learned skill: 我會開車. 能 is being able in the circumstances: 我今天能來. 可以 is permission: 我可以走嗎. All three go before the verb. 會 can also mean something will happen.

title: 幾 and 多少 ask how many
short: 幾 for small numbers, 多少 for any.
body: Use 幾 when you expect a small number, with a measure word: 幾個人. Use 多少 for larger or unknown amounts, and the measure word is optional.

title: Measure words
body: Chinese can't put a number straight onto a noun: 三個人, three people. 個 is the general one. Specific ones like 本 for books come with the noun, and 這 and 那 take them too.

title: 太…了 means too or so
body: 太好了 is great, and 太貴了 is too expensive. It carries feeling, so it can be pleased or complaining depending on the adjective.

title: 在 and 正在 for ongoing actions
short: 在 + verb means doing right now.
body: Before a verb with no place after it, 在 says an action is under way: 我在看書, I'm reading. 正在 stresses that it is happening at this very moment.

title: 過 for experience
short: Verb + 過 means have done before.
body: 過 says something has happened at least once in your life: 我去過中國, I've been to China. Negate it with 沒: 我沒去過.

title: 還 means still and also
body: 他還在睡覺, he is still sleeping. It can add something too: 我還要咖啡, I also want coffee. In questions, 還是 offers a choice: 茶還是咖啡, tea or coffee.

title: 因為…所以
body: Chinese gives the reason before the result, and can use both words together: 因為下雨，所以我不去, because it's raining, I'm not going. Either word can also appear alone.

title: 但是 and 可是 mean but
body: 他很忙，但是很高興, he is busy but happy. 雖然 can set up the contrast in the first clause: 雖然…但是.

title: 如果…就
body: 如果 opens the condition and 就 sits before the verb of the result: 如果下雨，我就不去. 就 goes after the subject of the second clause.

title: 比 compares
body: 他比我高, he is taller than me. Never put 很 before the adjective in a 比 sentence. To say how much, add it at the end: 他比我高一點兒.

title: 給 marks who receives
body: 給 means give, but before a verb it marks who the action is for: 我給你打電話, I'll phone you. The person comes before the action, unlike English.

title: 跟 and 和 mean with
body: 我跟他一起去, I'm going with him. 和 also joins nouns: 我和你, you and me. It doesn't join whole sentences the way "and" does in English.

title: 得 describes how an action goes
body: 他跑得很快, he runs fast. If there is an object, say the verb twice: 他說中文說得很好. It's a different word from 的, though both are often pronounced de.

title: 著 for lasting states
short: Verb + 著 means in that state.
body: 門開著, the door is open. 他坐著看書, he reads while sitting. It describes a situation that continues rather than an event.

title: 就 and 才
short: 就 is sooner than expected, 才 is later.
body: 他八點就來了, he came as early as eight. 他八點才來, he didn't come until eight. They place a feeling on the timing.

title: 從…到 and 離
body: 從 marks a starting point: 從北京到上海, from Beijing to Shanghai. 離 gives the distance from somewhere: 我家離學校很近, my home is close to school.

title: 把 moves the object forward
body: 把 is for saying what you did to a specific thing and how it ended up: 我把書放在桌子上, I put the book on the table. The verb can't stand alone; something must follow it.

title: 被 for the passive
body: 我的手機被他拿走了, my phone was taken by him. It often describes something unwelcome, and the doer can be left out.

title: 已經 and 快…了
body: 已經 goes before the verb, usually with 了: 他已經走了. 快…了 says something is about to happen: 快下雨了, it's about to rain.

title: 連…都 for emphasis
short: Even: 連 + thing + 都 + verb.
body: 他連水都不喝, he doesn't even drink water. It stresses that something is an extreme case.

title: 越…越
body: 越來越好 means better and better. 他越說越快, the more he talks, the faster he goes.

title: 只要 and 只有
short: As long as, and only if.
body: 只要 sets a sufficient condition with 就: 只要努力就行. 只有 sets the only condition with 才: 只有努力才行.

title: 不但…而且
body: 她不但聰明，而且很努力, she is not only clever but also hard-working. The second clause adds to the first.
